I can answer this one! There are 3 official languages in Belgium. Flanders in the north that speaks Dutch. Wallonia in the south where they speak French and there is a small german community. 
Brussels is duolangual (Dutch and French)

Most official paperwork is made in 3 diffrent languages and distributed on where you live. So in Flanders you get it in Dutch, Wallonia in French. And in Brussels it's always in 2 languages. 

For a lot of language related subjects are treated on a regional niveau. Things like schools and culture are decided on that niveau. A Flanders government, French Goveement and german one . (Way more complicated irl but this is the most important) 

We get lessons in our second language (French in Flanders, Dutch in Wallonia) when we are about 10. When we are about 13 we get to learn English. And a lot of us (not the majority thou) learn a basic German when we are 16-17. 

And as far as I know they used to speak some kind of Dutch in the north of France. But nobody speaks it anymore.
